But, this is a good complex nonetheless. It will burn a lot of calories for half an hour's worth of exercise, although exactly how many will vary for each individual. In general, the bigger and more muscular you are, the more calories you will burn for any given workout. A 250 lb man who's more muscle than fat could expect to burn about 600-700 calories with this. Also, for weight loss purposes it's better to just ignore any calories burned from cardio anyways. So keep that in mind.

If you have a pair of light dumbbells you got at a garage sale that you don't know what to do with, you're going to like this. If you need a form of cardio that you can do inside without having to buy a $1000 rowing machine or a $2000 stairclimber, you'll like this too. If you want a p90x style cardio workout you can do without having to buy an expensive TV or some highly overpriced DVDs and staring at the TV like a dope for an hour, you'll really love this.

I came up with this because I've found that most dumbbell workouts try to be a combination of cardio and strength training. There are also some good ones that are pure strength [for example, the "dumbbell stopgap" program in the sidebar. Did you write that, /u/nilceps?], but really none that are pure cardio, and thus won't leave you too beat up and sore to do your regular strength work the next day. This is that one. This is so purely cardio that you can do it on the very same day, after your strength training if you want. Use it like you would use a run, when you can't [or don't want to] actually go for a run, basically.

How to do it, in one paragraph- Get some light dumbbells. Take one, clasp your fingers under the weight part, and do kettlebell-style swings with it. If you don't know how to do kettlebell swings, go watch a video on it, there's too much going on to explain in words. Do that for five minutes. After five minutes, immediately pick up both dumbbells and begin doing clean and presses. The clean should be a clean, not a cheated biceps curl. The press should be a push press; most of the force should come from your legs and core. Don't ignore this, or it won't be the full-body cardio it's meant to be, and it'll make you sore. After five minutes of that, immediately go back to swings. Repeat three times for a half-hour workout.

Tips:

  • The intensity should be similar to a rowing machine or a jog. If it's harder than that, get a lighter set of dumbbells and don't go so hard.

  • Use light dumbbells. This is meant to be cardio, don't forget it. 15-20 lbs should be good for a man, unless you're half gorilla, and 5-10 for a woman, unless your name is Rhonda Rousey.

  • If you don't have light dumbbells, check at a garage sale, they're everywhere. If you can't afford them, steal them.
